entries.275f61e5336f97a7: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥163,643 million, up 18.3% from the previous year. The securities report states, “We have updated the all-time high.” By segment, the Sporting Goods Business accounted for ¥163,091 million (badminton goods ¥101,707 million, tennis goods ¥21,983 million, golf goods ¥1,460 million, other goods ¥37,939 million), and the Sports Facilities Business for ¥552 million. According to the company, demand for badminton goods was firm, centered on Asia, its main market; brand recognition for tennis goods rose through the performance of contracted players at international tournaments; and other goods such as wear and bags also expanded their global sales. Note that the sales subsidiaries in China, Taiwan, North America, Germany and the United Kingdom and the manufacturing subsidiaries in India and Thailand consolidate results for January to December 2025, so their period differs from the filing company’s fiscal year ended March 2026.
entries.3d2aaf6bd3b7ecc5: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥16,546 million (up 16.7% from the previous year), ordinary profit was ¥16,316 million (up 16.8%), and profit attributable to owners of parent was ¥12,092 million (up 14.2%); the securities report states that the company recorded record-high profit.
entries.60a0799d37f0eb19: YONEX CO., LTD. (the company) and 8 [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] make up the group. The eight are YONEX CORPORATION in the United States, YONEX U.K. LIMITED in the United Kingdom, YONEX GmbH in Germany, YONEX SPORTS(CHINA)CO.,LTD. in China, YONEX TAIWAN CO.,LTD. in Taiwan, YONEX INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED in India, YONEX TECNIFIBRE CO.,LTD. in Thailand, and Yonex Seiki Co., Ltd. in Japan. The securities report describes India and Thailand as manufacturing subsidiaries and lists Taiwan as a local corporation that carries out both manufacturing and sales. Its domestic manufacturing sites are the Niigata Plant (Nagaoka, Niigata Prefecture) and the Tokyo Plant (Soka, Saitama Prefecture), and its head office is in Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo. Of these, YONEX SPORTS(CHINA)CO.,LTD. in China is listed in the securities report as a company whose revenue, excluding internal sales between consolidated companies, was ¥80,692 million, accounting for more than 10% of consolidated revenue. Consolidated headcount at the end of the fiscal year ended March 2026 was 2,980 employees (in addition, an average of 674 temporary employees).

entries.6378bdff375ee083: This is the core business of the company group, manufacturing and selling sporting goods for badminton, tennis, golf and other sports. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥163,091 million, accounting for most of consolidated revenue of ¥163,643 million. Revenue by product category was: badminton equipment ¥101,707 million, tennis equipment ¥21,983 million, golf equipment ¥1,460 million, and other equipment, including wear and bags, ¥37,939 million. Manufacturing is carried out at domestic manufacturing sites and also at local subsidiaries in Asia (Taiwan, India and Thailand). Sales are handled by the company in Japan and, overseas, by local subsidiaries and leading distributors in each country. The securities report discloses this business divided into 4 reportable segments by region (Japan, Asia, North America and Europe), based on the sales structure.
entries.707d325d332de01a: This segment is handled by local subsidiaries in Europe (the United Kingdom and Germany), and the consolidated subsidiaries are YONEX U.K. LIMITED and YONEX GmbH. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥6,077 million (up 13.4% year on year), and operating profit was ¥506 million (up 6.2% year on year). The securities report explains that badminton equipment grew due to heightened interest in the sport from the hosting of international tournaments, among other factors, and tennis rackets grew due to improved brand recognition from the performance of sponsored players.

entries.af033f9c00d8bc0b: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥16,546 million (up 16.7% from the previous year), ordinary profit was ¥16,316 million (up 16.8%), and profit attributable to owners of parent was ¥12,092 million (up 14.2%); the securities report states that the company recorded record-high profit. According to the company, although raw material prices rose and currency effects were felt, higher revenue increased gross profit, and this exceeded the increase in selling, general and administrative expenses, such as advertising and personnel costs, arising from marketing investment to expand brand recognition and revitalize the market. Ordinary profit was affected by foreign exchange losses, among other factors. Operating profit of the reportable segments (before adjustments) was ¥11,864 million in Asia, ¥3,962 million in Japan, ¥506 million in Europe and ¥256 million in North America; North America fell 54.2% from the previous year, due in part to costs of its DTC initiatives. The Sports Facilities Business posted an operating loss of ¥22 million (it had operating profit of ¥16 million in the previous year).
entries.af2baf0311e98b0a: The company manufactures badminton rackets, soft tennis rackets, tennis rackets (hard tennis), golf clubs, snowboards, shuttlecocks, strings and so on. Some badminton rackets, shuttlecocks and other products are sourced from YONEX SPORTS(CHINA)CO.,LTD. in China and YONEX TAIWAN CO.,LTD. in Taiwan, tennis balls from YONEX TECNIFIBRE CO.,LTD., and stringing machines from Yonex Seiki Co., Ltd.; it also purchases and sells products such as wear and shoes. Production for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥50,256 million (at standard selling prices, including transfers between segments), and purchases were ¥68,011 million (at purchase prices). R&D expenses were ¥2,692 million, and the securities report states that in the same period the company developed and launched, as the result of about 15 years of research and development, a shuttlecock made from artificial material (product name CROSSWIND 70) and the VCORE series of tennis rackets, among others. Its management policy states that it will strengthen proposals of “Head to Toe” (from head to toe), offering rackets, shoes, wear and other products together.

entries.bbd56525b0af9345: This business operates golf courses, golf driving ranges and tennis clubs, and is conducted solely by the company in Japan. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥552 million (down 0.8% year on year), and operating loss was ¥22 million (operating profit of ¥16 million in the prior year). The securities report explains that at the core Yonex Country Club, although affected by intense summer heat and winter snow, the number of visitors increased and revenue rose slightly, while at other facilities revenue fell due to operating restrictions and other effects of poor weather. The loss is stated to be due to increased facility repair costs and other factors.
